Update: Nov 4th, 2026 11:23 EST 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google Real Madrid face AEK Athens in the Champions League on Wednesday, and while the Spanish giants need no introduction, their Greek opponents have a name that continues to leave more than a few fans scratching their heads. Come on, if you’re reading this, you’re one of them!
 Well, the letters ‘AEK’ stand for Athlitiki Enosis Konstantinoupoleos , which translates as “Athletic Union of Constantinople.” 
 Yes, Constantinople. Not Athens. Let me continue...
 Why is AEK Athens named after Constantinople?
 The explanation goes back to 1924, when Greek refugees and migrants from Constantinople, now Istanbul, established the club in Athens following the upheaval of the Greco-Turkish War. You didn’t expect a history lesson, right?
 Founded on April 13 of that year, AEK became much more than a soccer team. It represented a community determined to preserve its cultural identity and connection to its former homeland.
 What does the AEK Athens badge represent?
 This history also explains the club’s distinctive black-and-yellow colors and double-headed eagle , a symbol associated with the Byzantine Empire.
